patch_description: Replace the ad-hoc concentric-ring layout (which only achieves sum ≈ 0.96) with a proper hexagonal lattice arrangement: rows of 5,4,5,4,5,3 circles with hexagonal vertical spacing (√3·r) and staggered columns — the classic densest local structure for circle packing. With 6 rows, the equal radius that fits the unit square is r ≈ 1/(2+5√3) ≈ 0.0939, giving sum ≈ 2.44 immediately. Then, because square corners leave extra space that a pure hex lattice wastes, I add a greedy expansion phase: repeatedly sweep over circles and grow each one to the maximum radius allowed by the walls and its current neighbors (min over wall distances and d_ij - r_j). This is always feasible (each step keeps the packing valid) and monotonically increases the sum, letting corner/edge circles bulge into the leftover corner space — moving the sum toward the 2.635 AlphaEvolve target.
